descriptionModule.briefSummary: The aim of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of homohartonine combined with venetoclax and azacitidine (HVA) versus intensive chemotherapy (IA/DA) or venetoclax combined with azacitidine (VA) in newly diagnosed high-risk AML patients.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: The HVA regimen exerts a synergistic pro-apoptotic effect and has demonstrated significant clinical efficacy against R/R AML and also overcomes adaptive resistance observed in the VA regimen. Exploratory work with small sample sizes in first-line settings suggests that combination of HHT and Ven+AZA exhibits potent anti-AML effects with good safety profiles, particularly in overcoming the impact of high-risk factors associated with AML relative to standard treatments. This indicates its potential as a more ideal option for the treatment of newly diagnosed AML with high risk factors. Therefore a prospective, multi-center, randomized controlled clinical study is planned to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the HVA regimen compared to intensive chemotherapy (IA/DA) or Venetoclax plus azacitidine (VA) regimens in newly diagnosed high-risk fit-AML or unfit AML patients.

conditions: Newly Diagnosed Acute Myeloid Leukemia With High Risk

designInfo.interventionModelDescription: Patients with newly diagnosed AML with high risk will be divided into two cohorts, including patients being eligible for intensive chemotherapy and those with unfit status according to Ferrara 2013 criteria. In the fit cohort, patients will be randomized into accepting HVA versus IA/DA for induction with a ratio of 1:1. In the unfit cohort, patients will be randomized into accepting HVA versus VA for induction with a ratio of 1:1.

interventions.name: HVA
interventions.description: Homoharringtonine (HHT) is given by venous drip daily at 1 mg/m2 from day 1 to 7. Venetoclax (VEN) is given 100 mg on day 1, 200 mg on day 2, and 400 mg orally from day 3 to day 14. Azacitidine (AZA) is given 75 mg/m2 subcutaneously from day 1 to 7.

interventions.name: VA
interventions.description: VEN is given 100 mg on day 1, 200 mg on day 2, and 400 mg orally from day 3 to day 28, and AZA (75 mg/m2) is given subcutaneously from day 1 to 7.

interventions.name: Standard Chemotherapy
interventions.description: Standard Chemotherapy includes IA(Idarubicin combined with Cytarabine) or DA(Daunorubicin combined with Cytarabine). IDA is given by venous drip daily at 12mg/m2, or DNR is given by venous drip daily at 60mg/m2, from day 1-3, combined with Ara-C at 100mg/m2 by continuously venous drip from day 1-7.

primaryOutcomes.description: CRc includes complete remission (CR) and complete remission accompanied with with incomplete count recovery (CRi).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At the end of cycle 2 (each cycle is 28 days).

secondaryOutcomes.description: Complete remission is defined as BM with \>5% blasts and without extramedullary infltration and recovery of peripheral blood cells.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At the end of cycle 2 (each cycle is 28 days).

secondaryOutcomes.description: ORR includes CRc, partial response (PR), and morphologic leukemia-free state (MLFS).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At the end of cycle 2 (each cycle is 28 days).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Rate of Measurable residual disease (MRD) negative
secondaryOutcomes.description: MRD is monitored using flow cytometric analysis with a positive MRD threshold of 0.1%.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At the end of cycle 2 (each cycle is 28 days).

secondaryOutcomes.description: OS is calculated from enrollment to death or the last follow-up.
EFS is calculated from enrollment to the date of relapse or death or the last follow-up.
AE are recorded from the first dose until 28 days after treatment discontinuation and are graded according to the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: The first dose until 28 days after treatment discontinuation
